expected: The published event stands; the snapshot is rebuilt and no effect is applied twice.
A parse or hash failure stops the run; nothing is filled in as a successful event.
Resending the same result ID is idempotent; no second CREATE or repair.
A compare-and-set conflict is refused, and the caller reads the latest state.
The later writer fails to take the lock; shared files are never changed at the same time.
A lease is never taken on the clock alone.
An approval whose scope digest differs is not reused.
A host_observed claim in arbitrary JSON is not treated as an observed host event.
Another run's verify.json is never used as final evidence.
A stage handover is kept apart from a command's success; final completion stays unmet.
accepted_with_debt is not allowed; the run is blocked.
A legitimate RED is accepted and the run moves on to implementation.
Not counted as RED but as UNRUN; the run goes to a seam or environment repair.
The run returns to the parent stage and implements only after a real RED.
Story authoring appends the missing example. The covered example stays annotated and keeps its prior evidence, and no annotated example loses its test.
A claimed test-defect fix that changes what the expectation means is refused and returned to SDD.
The RED of the old tree is kept; a legitimate GREEN change alone never makes RED be taken again.
The test and implementation receipts that depend on it are invalidated.
A change in a glob's member set is found even when every existing file's hash is unchanged.
The run does not wait as if saturated; it stops as unavailable.
New dispatches and writes stop; a review that never ran is not reported as PASS.
The lock and paths of one file are never mistaken for another, and writes outside the root are prevented.
The user's settings are not overwritten, and the semantic conflict is reported.
The baseline tool's gate is kept apart from the candidate test, and a self-weakened gate never passes.
